_: How a field battle plays (army_field.gd, army_melee.gd and combat.gd read it through data.gd; docs/TUNING.md). kickLands: a kick's chance to land. dodge: the chance a blow that misses is a dodge rather than a parry. kickOdds: how often a swordsman kicks instead of cutting. floored: the chance a heavy blow that doesn't kill knocks a man down. field: the massed battle of two hosts (army_field.gd on army.gd's regiments): gap, the lines' middles apart when they deploy; start, seconds both lines stand before it begins; advance, the foot's pace to contact (units a second); contact, the gap between front ranks at blows; overlap, how much of two fronts must face each other across the line before they are at blows (share of their blocks' half widths together; a regiment off to the side closes square on its foe's front first); longest, seconds at blows before the beaten break whatever their strength. volley: seconds between an archer regiment's volleys (low, high), arrows in one, their flight (seconds) and arc (height over distance), men it fells (low, high), and how near the lines may come before archers stop (until). fight: men a regiment in contact loses a second (beaten, victors; the outcome is the realm's, Freeciv's), seconds between a front man's blows (low, high), the chance a front man reels instead (hitOdds) or takes a blow on his shield (blockOdds), ranks that fight, how far the front surges, how much harder a flanked regiment bleeds, and seconds between the dust its front throws up at blows (dustEvery). cavalry: ride and charge pace, how far round the enemy's end it swings (wide), how far behind its front it turns in (behind), and the men its charge fells at once where it strikes (shock). waver: strength below which a beaten regiment's banner wavers; rout: below which it breaks; run: its pace in flight; scatter: how far each running man drifts a second; fade: seconds before the routed are gone. camera: the lens's quarter off the lines and how fast it follows. field.play: battles in play (scenes.gd stages one where the bridge tells of a battle, always): the lines' middles apart there, men in a regiment for each company that fought, the most companies shown a side, how many such battles at once (more are told, not shown), seconds the field stays held before it's gone, kinds: the companies [beaten, victors] of a battle staged where no scene named them (the film's, the shot harness's). field.turns: bearings tried round the crown's muster for the foe's line, the one on the most fit ground taken; field.frontage: men abreast in a battle regiment (low, high), deeper blocks than the muster's line. ground.*: where a battle may be fought (battlefield): field (how far the fight reaches from its centre), rise (the most the ground may rise or fall across the field), rings (how far out, in rings 0.8 apart, it is looked for), town_clear (how far its edge keeps from a town), farm_clear (its centre from a farmstead, past the field), rough (what each kind of land costs it).
